acceptanceCriteria: `corvint affected --base <607-path range>` output is byte-identical before and after on this repository and the existing affected/gateselect tests pass
affected readers() no longer performs a map lookup or loop-invariant string scan per (dirty path, unit, token); measured wall time on the HEAD~20 range retained (target <= 2 s, prototype 1.77 s)
gateselect Select's per-path reader attribution uses the existing pathMatcher (or a shared equivalent) and `corvint test --dry-run` CPU in reader matching is retained before/after
A benchmark or recorded measurement for both packages is retained with the change
body:
Measured 2026-10-18 on origin/main 6ceee260b (Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 668, darwin, load ~6), scratch clone, CPU profile from an overlay build.

`corvint affected --base HEAD~20` (607 dirty paths) takes 6.2 s single-threaded. 70% of samples are in Graph.readers -> namersWith -> namesAny: for every dirty path, every unit, every PathToken it calls runCache.of (map hash + memequal: 2.78 s of 4.35 s) and then namesPathRuns, which recomputes the loop-invariant strings.HasPrefix(value,"/") / strings.Contains(value,"..") per run (0.67 s). HEAD~5 (119 paths): 1.71 s, readers ~1.0 s.

Prototype (scratch overlay, not committed): precompute each unit's token runs once per readers() call into a [][]tokenRun indexed by graph.order and hoist the file-name-only flag into it. Result: 6.20 s -> 1.77 s on 607 paths with byte-identical JSON output (cmp), 1.71 -> 1.62 s on 119 paths. readers then costs 0.8 s.

Further step: internal/gateselect already has pathMatcher (inverted component index over all dirty paths, readers.go:637) for the bound-lines path, but Select still calls index.attribute -> readers -> namesPath per dirty path (0.66 s of 5.1 s CPU in `corvint test --base HEAD~5 --dry-run`), re-running componentRuns and strings.Split per call over every holder. Both affected.readers and gateselect.attribute can evaluate all dirty paths per token at once through a pathMatcher-style index; the ascending path indices keep the smallest-naming-dirty-path witness rule. Note the two namesPath copies differ (affected applies the V1-0290 file-name-only rule for lone components; gateselect's does not), so a shared matcher must keep each relation.
title: affected and gateselect: path-literal reader matching is O(dirty x units x tokens) with a map lookup per step; 607-path affected takes 6.2 s, 1.8 s with precomputed runs
